subject: Control Tower: Northridge throughput & error-rate stabilization

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Cohen <eli.cohen@northridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control Tower: Northridge throughput & error-rate stabilization

Eli / Sarah —

Thanks for the quick call earlier. We see a sustained throughput spike on your region (us-west-2) that correlates with a jump in 5xxs from our serving layer and a growing tail latency for short requests. High-level:

- Spike started ~2026-04-26T08:40 PDT; peak qps ~3.7x baseline.
- Error-rate (5xx) increased from 0.3% to ~4.1% during the window.
- Throughput throttles observed when session concurrency crosses optimized pool limits.

Immediate ask: please send the Correlation ID and one representative session id (the one you flagged on the call). I've attached an initial perf snapshot from our control plane (northridge_perf_snapshot_20260426.pdf).

What we're doing now (short timeline):
- T+0-30m: triage and isolate hot model variant paths (Marissa + Ben).
- T+30-90m: apply temporary routing to a lower-latency compatible variant and enable prefix caching for high-frequency prefixes (Grace).
- T+90-180m: apply capacity bump from Dedicated pool and validate regressions against your golden prompt set.

I'll run a concise executive readout after we confirm the first mitigation (routing change) so your execs have a single point update. Please confirm if Northridge wants a DocuSign-approved MOP for the capacity bump or if verbal approval is fine for today.

Jordan
Jordan Blake

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control Tower: Northridge throughput & error-rate stabilization

Holding notes from infra triage (short):

- Root cause hypothesis: model-variant KV cache thrash + bursty session fanout causing GPU context-switch overhead. Two model variants show cache miss ratio > 0.6 on the hot prefixes.
- Quick mitigation path: route traffic for high-frequency endpoints to variant-v2 (quantized) that has smaller KV working set and lower tail latency. Impact estimate: reduce 95th p90 by ~40-55% for affected flows.
- Risk: quantized variant occasionally shows small semantic drift on long-form prompts; we've validated against Northridge's 12 golden prompts with no regressions so far. Full regression suite is running (ETA 75m).

I've attached a fast mutual action plan draft (mutual_action_plan_Northridge_v3.docx) with owner/time commitments — please review. Ben / Grace, can you confirm we have capacity headroom in the Dedicated pool to add +12% for the next 3 hours? If yes, Jordan can request verbal bump from Northridge.

Marissa Cole
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: mutual_action_plan_Northridge_v3.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Cohen <eli.cohen@northridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control Tower: Northridge throughput & error-rate stabilization

Eli —

Quick update for Northridge execs and ops leadership:

- What we changed (T+45m): traffic routing rule applied to route high-frequency prefixes to variant-v2; prefix caching enabled on the hot prefixes; temporary +12% Dedicated capacity allocated.
- Immediate effect: 5xxs dropped from ~4.1% to ~0.9% within 8 minutes post-change; p95 latency reduced from 820ms -> 470ms for affected short requests.
- Next steps (T+90-180m): full regression results, validate golden prompts, monitor for tail reappearance, and hold a 30-minute exec readout at 14:30 PDT if useful.

Please consider this the single-threaded executive update you can share with stakeholders. If your execs want a one-pager, we can produce a two-slide summary and signal the recommended next steps: (1) keep routing in place for 24 hours, (2) schedule a follow-up debrief with product to discuss variant promotion.

Verbal approval logged per Eli's note; we'll proceed with the capacity bump for the window discussed.

Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
